title: Build an AI Analyst You Can Trust

slides.title: Two people
slides.body:
One makes demos. Impressive for a week. Trusted with nothing real.

One makes things a team runs on. Looks boring. Gets the budget.

Same tools. One habit apart.
slides.notes: Cast the room: PM, eng lead, exec. Same move tonight: you are hiring a teammate and deciding whether to trust it.

slides.title: Three names. Four numbers. One habit.
slides.body:
Eval: did it do the job. Guardrail: did it avoid harm. Governance: can you prove it to someone who was not in the room.

Groundedness 3 of 4. Completion yes. Cost $0.11. Speed 19s.

You do not test it once. You check every run.
slides.notes: Groundedness is the one nobody tracks and the one that ends careers. Then teach the SHAPE of evals over the next three slides — that is the depth a senior room paid for.

slides.title: What goes wrong isn't the model lying.
slides.body:
• Fabrication — a fact with no source at all
• Drift — a real source, bent to a number it never said
• Omission — the counter-evidence it left out
• Silent regression — a model update quietly breaks it
slides.notes: These are shapes, not evil. Drift is the dangerous one — it survives a careful read. You cannot check for a failure you have not named. This maps to the taxonomy on /trust/evals.

slides.title: Let a model judge — carefully.
slides.body:
• It prefers longer answers
• It prefers its own phrasing
• It can be wrong the same way the writer is
• So the check that matters stays code, not a chat
slides.notes: A model-as-judge scales to nuance code can't reach — but it has biases: position, verbosity, self-preference, correlated error. Use it to rank and triage, calibrate it against humans first, and never let it gate the safety-critical path. This is the whole reason tonight's gate was sixty lines of Python.

slides.title: What even a perfect gate misses.
slides.body:
• A real source bent to the wrong conclusion
• The counter-evidence it never cited
• A reasoning error built on sound facts
• So a human still signs
slides.notes: No single eval covers these — that is why it is a SUITE, plus human judgment. The gate removes the failure humans are worst at: the confident, well-sourced, wrong number. It does not replace the human; it frees them for the failures only judgment catches. Full map: /trust/evals.

slides.title: You already knew how to make the trick.
slides.body:
Now you are the person who can be trusted with it.

Every fact carries the sentence it came from.
Something goes and checks.

khaledzaky.com/trust
